questions.prompt: According to the book, what is a context window best compared to?
questions.rationale: "A context window is not a memory; it is a desk, and desks get cluttered."

questions.prompt: What does the book call packaged, on-demand expertise the model can load?
questions.rationale: "A skill is expertise the model didn't have to be trained on -- it just had to be told where to look."

questions.prompt: In one sentence, why does the harness delegate work to subagents?
questions.model_answer: To hand off wide exploration to a separate clean-context worker so the main conversation doesn't get cluttered.
questions.rationale: "Delegation meant giving a piece of the problem to a version of yourself that would not remember trying."

questions.prompt: How does the book describe the shift in how permissions are designed?
choices: From a map to a single switch
From a single switch to a blast-radius map
questions.rationale: "Permissions stopped being a single on/off switch and became a map of blast radius."

questions.prompt: What lets the harness keep working after a person stops watching it?
questions.rationale: "The most useful version of the harness was the one still working after everyone had stopped watching it."
